assessment.nobel_worthiness: A highly consequential framework linking firm-level distortions to aggregate productivity and international income differences.
assessment.attribution: The three credited researchers represent a coherent and identifiable contribution spanning measurement, theory and quantitative application.
assessment.maturity: The research programme is well established and has strongly shaped work on development, productivity and policy.
uncertainties: The empirical magnitude and policy interpretation of measured misallocation remain debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection transformed modern trade theory and empirical analysis of trade gains.
assessment.attribution: Melitz supplies the central benchmark, while Helpman and Redding are integral to its extension and broader trade implications.
assessment.maturity: Its mechanisms, empirical relevance and policy implications have been extensively developed over two decades.
uncertainties: The breadth of related contributors makes a three-person attribution necessarily selective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The financial-accelerator and collateral-constraint approach fundamentally changed macroeconomic analysis of credit cycles.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore provide the core collateral mechanism, with Gertler central to its macroeconomic financial-accelerator development.
assessment.maturity: The contribution has endured through successive financial episodes and is embedded in modern macro-finance.
uncertainties: Credit-cycle research has several adjacent foundational strands and a limited laureate allocation cannot cover all of them.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evolutionary analysis of routines, capabilities and organizational change offered a durable alternative lens on economic dynamism.
assessment.attribution: Winter is a clear central figure in the credited contribution.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have generated a long-running interdisciplinary research tradition and broad influence.
uncertainties: The listed formulation omits important collaborators and creates an attribution-boundary question.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on reciprocity, fairness and inequity aversion materially revised economic models of individual interaction.
assessment.attribution: Fehr and Schmidt anchor the canonical theoretical and experimental contribution, with Falk an important associated contributor.
assessment.maturity: The programme is mature, extensively replicated and influential across labour, organizational and behavioural economics.
uncertainties: The generality of laboratory and field measures of social preferences remains contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The political-economy analysis of trade policy supplied a powerful explanation for protection beyond representative-agent welfare models.
assessment.attribution: Grossman and Helpman are unmistakably associated with the central theoretical framework.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been a standard reference point for decades in research on trade and lobbying.
uncertainties: Empirical adjudication among competing political explanations for trade policy is incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression created a foundational toolkit for studying heterogeneous relationships and distributional outcomes.
assessment.attribution: Koenker and Bassett are the direct and clearly identifiable originators of the core method.
assessment.maturity: The method is long established and broadly used throughout economics and adjacent disciplines.
uncertainties: Its methodological importance may be viewed as less transformative for economic science than the leading substantive programmes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian models substantially improved analysis of monetary and fiscal transmission across households.
assessment.attribution: The three credited economists form a coherent group behind influential quantitative frameworks and applications.
assessment.maturity: The approach is now central in policy-oriented macroeconomics and has accumulated substantial follow-on evidence.
uncertainties: The literature is comparatively recent and its long-run empirical and policy robustness remains to be fully assessed.
